answer: A coral reef guards an agent economy with square-number diving: every new identity must dive to a deeper reef terrace and fetch one opal, and the depth follows the squares, so the first fake dives 1 fathom, the second 4, the third 9, the tenth 100 and the twentieth 400, and twenty fakes together dive 2,870 fathoms. Bulk farming fails because one diver makes one dive at a time and each terrace must be reached before the next is attempted, so no dive can be split in parallel or bought; like a signal fading with the square of distance, the cost of the next fake always outruns the last.
